claim: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disease on the oral mucosa of unknown etiology mediated by T cells with a 1.01% global prevalence rate.
source: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disease on the oral mucosa of unknown etiology mediated by T cells with a 1.01% global prevalence rate (González-Moles et al., 2021; Jiang et al., 2022b).
evidence: Supported by citations to González-Moles et al., 2021 and Jiang et al., 2022b

claim: EOLP has a significantly higher risk of malignant transformation than NEOLP.
source: Notably, EOLP has a significantly higher risk of malignant transformation than non-erosive oral lichen planus (NEOLP) (Arduino et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Arduino et al., 2021

claim: The pathological feature of OLP is characterized by dense infiltration of T cells in the lamina propria, disruption of the basement membrane, and degeneration of basal keratinocytes.
source: The pathological feature of OLP is characterized by dense infiltration of T cells in the lamina propria, disruption of the basement membrane, and degeneration of basal keratinocytes (Xu et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xu et al., 2022

claim: OLP patients have immune function disorders both locally and systemically, with the infiltration of CD8+ T cells in the OLP lamina propria near the basement membrane.
source: Previous studies have shown that OLP patients have immune function disorders both locally and systemically, with the infiltration of CD8+ T cells in the OLP lamina propria near the basement membrane (Neppelberg et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Neppelberg et al., 2001

claim: CD8+ T cells are related to the liquefaction of basal cells in OLP.
source: CD8+ T cells are related to the liquefaction of basal cells, and it is believed that the immune microenvironment of OLP lesions has changed, especially in CD8+ T cells, which produce a complex network of cytokines and chemokines, such as IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL1α, and IL17, among others (Firth et al., 2015; Ke et al., 2017; Piccinni et al., 2014; Shaker and Hassan, 2012; Viguier et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies (Firth et al., 2015; Ke et al., 2017; Piccinni et al., 2014; Shaker and Hassan, 2012; Viguier et al., 2015)

claim: CD8+ T cells in OLP produce a complex network of cytokines and chemokines, such as IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL1α, and IL17.

evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies (Firth et al., 2015; Ke et al., 2017; Piccinni et al., 2014; Shaker and Hassan, 2012; Viguier et al., 2015)

claim: Tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells are a recently described population of terminally differentiated T cells, which are crucial for local immunity.
source: Tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells are a recently described population of terminally differentiated T cells, which are crucial for local immunity (Mueller et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mueller et al., 2014

claim: CD8+ Trm cells can persist locally for a long time in the absence of relevant antigens.
